_doc: 06 §3 and §5 — the drafted perk catalogue, reworked around nine ELEMENTAL AND GENERIC CATEGORIES, each gated behind a single base perk. THE GATE IS THE DESIGN. Every category authors exactly one perk with an empty `requires` — its base — and every other perk in that category requires it. A run that has not taken Ignite is never offered a Burn upgrade, because an offer a player can take and feel nothing from is worse than no offer at all. Rules.Perks.PerkDraftEngine enforces it by narrowing the draftable pool, the same way every other 06 §4 composition rule is enforced, so an unsatisfiable narrowing falls through instead of emptying a draft. The base perks are the nine COMMON rows; COMMON is the band they DRAW in and the empty `requires` is what makes them the entry, because 06 §4's RarityWeights are keyed on four bands and a fifth would be a weight table nobody wrote. THE FIVE ELEMENTS ARE FIVE STACKING RULES, which is what keeps them apart: LIGHTNING carries no ailment at all and is hit COUNT (arcs to further enemies, second strikes on the same one); COLD chills, which degrades what an enemy deals, and freezes, which stops it acting; FIRE burns on a capped stack that expires; POISON stacks without a cap and never expires; BLEED stacks to a cap, scales on the target's missing health, and is the one ailment a perk can SPEND for an instant payout (PK_REND). Ailment damage is a percentage of the applier's ATK across all three DoTs — see 05 §5 — so a poison build gains from the same items an attack build does. THE FOUR GENERIC CATEGORIES carry fewer rows than the five specific ones, on purpose: defence, offence, crit and sustain are what every build wants, and a wide generic pool would crowd out the elemental identity the draft is supposed to be building towards. HYBRIDS require SEVERAL bases and are filed under one of their categories — the category key is single-valued because 06 §4's diversity rule counts categories per draft, and a perk counted twice would satisfy a diversity narrowing on its own. Their `requires` list is where the multi-element demand actually lives. 🔒 ZERO PER-PERK CODE, unchanged from the original catalogue: every effect below is DSL data (18 §1) validated per-op against schema/effect.schema.json by DeclaredRules' R35, read by Content.Perks.PerkEffects and applied by the same interpreter every other effect source uses. ⚠️ Conditions read the effect's HOLDER, not its target (Rules.Effects.Conditions.ConditionEvaluator), so no perk here gates on 'is this ENEMY chilled' or scales on the target's ailment stacks — a sentence the vocabulary cannot say. Where the design wanted one, the perk applies its effect to the enemies it strikes instead, which is the same behaviour reached from the other side. Cursed Perks (06 §3.7) remain out of scope: they carry a Benefit/Cost shape, not tiers. 🔒 ONE ROW IS WITHHELD FROM THE DRAFT, and it is withheld HERE rather than in code: PK_ENDLESS_BLIGHT carries poolTags ["needs_run_state"] instead of ["standard"], because its valueScale reads BATTLES_WON_THIS_RUN and no fight composition supplies a run view yet — so the row is authored, schema-valid and unplayable: taking it ends the run at the next battle. PerkDraftEngine offers only rows tagged "standard", so restoring this one is this single edit and nothing else, on the day a fight carries the run's own state.
